shortDescription: Published (Workshop 3786107692, generation 5 shipped 2026-08-20). Shared foundation for the Radius UI suite: one colour set, one card/hover treatment, a shape module, a text field, a scroll widget, a font resolver, a world-map bake, a Perf module, and a 272-icon shared art library.
body:
## What this mod is

A **library mod**. It adds no defs, no world state, and no Harmony patches. It exists so the
Radius UI suite draws with one design language instead of many forked copies of one.

Design language: flat 2.0, rounded, iOS-like, colour-forward.

Architecture of record: `_dev/RadiusUIFramework/ARCHITECTURE.md` (human-owned). Nothing in
`_dev/` ships.

## Status: PUBLISHED (generation 5), in BUILD MODE

- **Steam Workshop: 3786107692.** First published 2026-08-18; generation 5 update shipped
  2026-08-20 (FlatField, Spatial, World, the token partials, `Need/` icons).
- **Git: `Astryls/Radius-UI-Framework`** (private), `main`. Autosave commits every 15 min.
- Licence: MIT. Author field is `astryl` (lowercase) by authorship, not by restamp.
- Build green, 0 warnings. No publish-hold outstanding.

Backups: `D:\Rimworld\Radius UI Framework\20260820-083608` (full folder, 502 files) and
`...\20260820-115330\Source`.

**Note: work done AFTER the 2026-08-20 publish is not yet on the Workshop** - currently the
overview-tab standard (`Metrics.Tabs` + `Panes/OverviewTab`).

## Publish protocol that worked (repeat this)

`_dev/publish-prep.ps1 -ModId RadiusUIFramework` then `_dev/publish-restore.ps1`. The tool takes
its own D: backup, disables `ModmixerGitAutosave`, and holds everything not on the runtime
allowlist. Four things worth remembering:

- **Delete genuine garbage BEFORE running prep.** The tool works off an allowlist, so anything
  unrecognised is *held* and faithfully *restored* later. A stray nested copy of the whole mod
  (tracked as gitlink 4f5fe71, carrying its own `.git`) had to be deleted first (commit
  f3540d1) or it would have come straight back.
- **`.modmixer/` must stay in place.** Moving it out makes Modmixer restamp About.xml's author
  to the lowercase default handle and re-serialize the description.
- **Restore in the same session.** Autosave is disabled during the window; had it fired it
  would have committed the stripped tree and deleted all source from HEAD.
- `.git` (1.8 MB, contains the private remote URL) is left in place by the tool by design,
  which conflicts with PUBLISH_CHECKLIST §6. Unresolved; only matters if the publish utility
  does not skip dotfolders.

## Texture library (272 icons, 19 categories)

Imported from five source mods. All byte-for-byte copies: no resampling, no recolouring.
Generation 5 added a `Need/` category (4 icons) pairing with `Palette.Needs`.

Namespaced under `Textures/RadiusUI/` because `ContentFinder` returns the *last-loaded* match,
so an un-namespaced sibling in a consumer would silently shadow it. Consumers must delete their
local copies, not merely stop referencing them.

### The art is three tiers, not one family

Only tier 1 can be re-themed:

- **Glyphs** - flat white RGB, all information in alpha. Tinted via `Palette`/accent.
- **Illustrations (`Anatomy/`)** - shaded beige art. Never tinted.
- **Semantic markers (`Marker/`)** - colour *is* the meaning; mapped to the semantic ramp. Hand
  synced to the palette: if the ramp changes, those 8 PNGs must be re-authored.

### Aliases are a hard requirement

12 retired names must stay exposed as aliases or consumer call sites break. `Squad/` ships 5
files but offers 8 emblem slots; `Reminder/` ships 7 but offers 8 picker slots.
`Action/LockOpen` and `Action/LockClosed` scored 0.927 similarity and were deliberately kept
apart - they are a **state pair**.

**No magnifier/search glyph exists**, deliberately: `FlatField` ships with no leading icon
rather than misusing `Action/EyeOpen`.

## Components

- `Tokens/` - `Palette` (+ Health, Ideology, Needs, Social, Bands partials), `Metrics`
  (+ Rows, Tabs partials). Pure values, no game state.
- `Chrome/` - `CardChrome` (the rounded card), `FlatField` (the text field), `Spatial`
  (+ Bands partial - the shape vocabulary).
- `Widgets/` - `FlatScroll`, `UIKit` (+ Bars partial).
- `Panes/OverviewTab` - standard tab footprint + live pane clamp.
- `Icons/` - `RadiusIcon` (art tier lives here), `IconSet` + generated per-tier partials.
- `Text/RadiusFont` - framework-owned font resolution and measurement.
- `World/WorldSnapshot` - real-terrain minimap bake + `TerritoryPaint`.
- `Settings/`, `Compat/ModCompat`, `Perf/`.

Several classes are `partial` (`Spatial`, `UIKit`, `Metrics`, `Palette`, `IconSet`) so
concurrent sessions add a **file** instead of editing a shared one. That is now the §13
recommendation and it is what let two sessions work this tree simultaneously.

### `Panes/OverviewTab` - the standard tab footprint (§17, §13 rule 6)

**Every module that replaces a vanilla overview tab renders at the same size** - Health, Needs,
Social, Bio/Character, Gear, Log, Training, and anything added later. Standard is
`Metrics.OverviewTabW` x `OverviewTabH` = **890 x 790** at scale 1, user scale clamped
**0.70-1.10** defaulting to **1.00**, height clamped against the live inspect pane.

These tabs share one inspect pane and players flip between them constantly, so a size
difference makes the pane appear to jump on every switch. The footprint is a property of the
*pane*, not of any one mod.

Audit that prompted it (2026-08-20): Health 890x790 @1.00 and Needs 890x790 @1.00 matched, but
**Social Tab had its axes transposed** (790x890 @0.85, rendering 672x756). Its own comment
stated the intent - "so the default lands on Health Tab's shipped footprint (672 x 756)" -
where Health's actual footprint at that scale is 756x672. Right numbers, swapped axes, in both
the constants and the comment describing them. Invisible in isolation, obvious side by side.

A constant alone is insufficient, so the helper owns two more things: the **clamp** (a bare 790
overflows at low resolution or high UI scale; the limit must come from live `PaneTopY` because
RimHUD and other pane mods raise it, and `UI.screenHeight` is already divided by `Prefs.UIScale`)
and the **default scale** (two tabs agreeing on constants but shipping different defaults still
render differently for every player who never opens settings). `MaxHeight` had been forked
verbatim three times.

**Hosted-tab trap:** a tab whose rect is owned by a host (Radius UI - Inspector) must use
`MaxHeightHosted(chromeH)`, never `MaxHeight`. The host sizes its panel from the declared tab
size then patches `PaneTopY` to report that panel's top, so clamping against `PaneTopY` clamps
against your own output - the two chase each other, identical constants end up different
heights, and the value changes on the frame hosting begins, which is the flicker.

Needs Tab's reflected read of Health Tab's *resolved* height is the belt-and-braces version of
this and should be left alone. It follows height only: Health's width grows with its side
flyout, and following that would make Needs jump for a reason unrelated to needs.

### `Chrome/FlatField` - the flat text field

`Draw(rect, text, controlName, placeholder, clearButton)` returns the edited text. Uplifted
from Faction Menu.

Framework-owned because it is **shared-GUIStyle surgery**. `Widgets.TextField` draws with
`Text.CurTextFieldStyle`, whose eight state backgrounds are vanilla's tan bevel, so a consumer's
own plate goes *under* vanilla chrome. The fix is a copy of that style with all eight
backgrounds nulled.

Four encoded rules: never mutate the shared style (`GUI.skin.textField` is a pure no-op here -
`Widgets.TextField` never reads it); copy from `Text.textFieldStyles[Small]`, not
`CurTextFieldStyle`, which resolves against ambient `Text.Font`; cache behind an epoch guard on
both the source style object and its font; `GUI.SetNextControlName` immediately before
`GUI.TextField` or focus detection silently never matches.

The clear button's `ButtonInvisible` and 24px reserve are emitted whenever `clearButton` is
true, not only when non-empty: an empty field can become non-empty between the input pass and
the Repaint pass of one frame, and a control appearing mid-frame renumbers every control the
caller draws after it.

### `Chrome/Spatial` - the shape module (§15)

What `CardChrome` structurally cannot draw. F1 established rounding does **not** need a
procedural 9-slice, but Unity's per-corner overload cannot do a shadow, disc, ring or capsule.
Ends a four-way fork; `BottomBand` alone had three. A lift of Modern Social Tab's
implementation, not a rewrite. Generated textures only, no shipped art.

Cost discipline: a 9-slice is nine draw calls - surfaces and row cards only; `Pill` is three;
faint row stripes stay square. `Pill` samples **half** discs by texcoord because whole discs
under a rect double-draw the caps (invisible at full alpha, three lumps below it). `BottomBand`
clips rather than shrinks, and registers nothing interactive inside the clip. All textures are
`HideAndDontSave` or `UnloadUnusedAssets` destroys them mid-session.

### `World/WorldSnapshot` - real-terrain minimap bake (§16)

Bounded BFS from a centre tile, rasterising each tile's actual polygon onto the tangent plane.
768² `Color32`, ~2.3 MB reused, ~5 ms upload, cached on centre/range/orientation/paint key.
Third occurrence of the technique, promoted unchanged so the copies cannot drift.

`TerritoryPaint` is **immutable** to the bake: a changed claim map must arrive as a new `Key` or
the cache returns a stale texture. Use `Transport` across a re-centre; deriving the basis from a
fixed world axis makes north swing and reads as the map rotating. Terrain colours are map
**content**, so this file does not route through `Palette`.

### `Perf/` - hot-path utilities

`FrameGate`, `Throttle`, `TextMemo`, `ScratchText`, `SnapshotTable`, `IdMap`,
`PooledWindowState`, `ViewCull`, `PatchGuard`, `DefTable`, `FrameProbe`. Main-thread only.
`RadiusFont.Size/Height/Width` route through `TextMemo` behind unchanged signatures.

## Binding rules for framework edits (§13)

Additive only; never change the value behind an existing name; missing token means add a new
one; **rebuild every consumer after any framework rebuild** and hash-verify their game-side
copies; the 12 icon aliases are permanent; **rule 6 - any vanilla-overview-tab replacement uses
`Panes/OverviewTab`**. Prefer a new `partial` file over editing a shared one. Framework
`Source/` receives concurrent pushes - always re-read a file from disk immediately before
editing it, **including ARCHITECTURE.md** (§1 was rewritten under a session mid-edit twice on
2026-08-20).

## Outstanding work (next session starts here)

1. **Social Tab must be re-pointed at the standard footprint** (§17). It currently renders
   672x756 against the standard 890x790. This is a visible size change for existing users, so
   it needs sign-off rather than a silent fix.
2. **Health and Needs should migrate to `Panes/OverviewTab`** to retire their private
   `MaxWindowH` copies. They already agree numerically, so there is no visible change.
3. **§13 rule 4 consumer sweep is owed.** The framework DLL changed materially. Every consumer
   must be rebuilt and their game-side copies hash-verified, or a consumer paired with an old
   DLL throws MissingMethodException.
4. **Game-side `RimWorld/Mods/RadiusUIFramework` is a real directory, not a symlink**, and its
   DLL has drifted stale. Consumers are symlinked and stay live, so the running game can pair
   new consumer DLLs with an old framework DLL. Needs a sync pass - most likely cause of any
   confusing runtime error, so clear it before testing.
5. **Faction Menu still carries two forks** the framework now owns: `Chrome/FlatField.cs`
   (redundant, pending deletion) and `Source/Core/WorldSnapshot.cs` (re-point at the framework
   copy). Deferred deliberately - that consumer is live and its StagePane wiring was unreviewed.
6. Generation 5 has had no clean-load test or Dubs performance sign-off.
7. About.xml `<description>` still describes the pre-generation-4 framework.
